description: This course covers static and dynamic analysis of malware using tools like IDA Pro, Ghidra, and Ghidra's decompiler; reverse engineering x86/x64 and ARM binaries with disassembly techniques; memory forensics with Volatility; malware behavior analysis using sandboxing and dynamic instrumentation; malware detection with YARA rules and static analysis; reverse engineering of PE and ELF file formats; malware persistence mechanisms; evasion techniques; and advanced analysis of ransomware and APT malware. The course also includes hands-on labs on malware unpacking, API hooking, and malware family classification.

clos.text: Define the fundamental concepts of reverse engineering and malware analysis, including static and dynamic analysis techniques and key tools such as IDA Pro and Ghidra.
Describe the structure and characteristics of PE and ELF file formats, including headers, sections, and relocation tables.
Explain the process of disassembling and decompiling x86/x64 and ARM binaries using advanced techniques such as control flow graph reconstruction.
Apply malware analysis techniques, including memory forensics with Volatility and dynamic instrumentation with Cuckoo Sandbox, to detect and analyze malicious behavior.
Implement a malware detection system using YARA rules and static analysis methods to classify and identify known and unknown malware families.

topics: Introduction to Reverse Engineering and Malware Analysis
Binary File Formats: PE and ELF
